assignments.title: 28.7 Quarter 4 Capstone: A Smaller World
assignments.html:
QUARTER 4 CAPSTONE
A Smaller World
One essay on the years from the Second World War to the present.
Capstone · 20 points · Word document upload
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
HOW TO WORK
Read your notes in My Notebook and look back over the quarter's lessons and primary sources first. Then write your essay in Word and submit it as the submission box below describes.
WHAT YOU ARE DOING

The Quarter 4 Capstone is one essay that brings the whole quarter together, from the Second World War to the opening years of this century. You will choose one of three questions, make an argument, and defend it with evidence from the lessons and the primary sources you have read.

CHOOSE ONE QUESTION
  1. Between 1945 and 1991 the two superpowers never fought each other directly. Was that mainly the work of wise leaders, of the fear of nuclear weapons, or of luck?
  2. What may a people do when its own government wrongs it, and what may other nations do about it? Defend your answer with at least two of the cases of the quarter, such as South Africa, the American South, Yugoslavia, or Eastern Europe in 1989.
  3. Did the great turning points of this quarter turn more on the choices of particular men and women, or on conditions they did not control?
WHAT YOUR ESSAY MUST DO

Write 800 to 1,200 words in Word. Give your essay a title. State your answer in the first paragraph, and keep it clear to the end.

  1. Use specific evidence from at least four different weeks of the quarter, naming people, decisions, and dates.
  2. Quote from at least two of the primary sources of the quarter. Put each quotation in quotation marks and cite it in a footnote.
  3. Include one counterfactual. Name a moment, say what might have gone differently, and say what you think would have followed.
  4. Answer the strongest objection to your view. Say what a thoughtful person on the other side would point to, and why you are still not persuaded.
  5. Say plainly what the evidence cannot show and what you are guessing.

Some of this quarter’s history involves great suffering. Write about it plainly and with respect. You will be graded on the quality of your argument, not on which question you choose or which side you take.

HOW YOUR CAPSTONE WILL BE SCORED (20 pts)
CriteriaExcellent (4)Proficient (3)Developing (2)Beginning (1)
Understanding of the material
5 pts		States the source’s claims and the lesson’s facts accurately and precisely, with short quotations used correctly.Accurate on the main points. Small gaps or loose wording.Partly accurate, or leans on summary instead of the source’s own words.Major errors, or little connection to the source and lessons.

The counterfactual is reasonable but thinly argued.Claims are asserted more than shown. The counterfactual is a guess with little support.Little reasoning, or the counterfactual is missing.

5 pts		Clear, organized, and exact. Each question is answered in its own labeled part.Mostly clear. Occasional vagueness or wandering.Hard to follow in places, or parts are missing.Unclear or disorganized.

Occasionally claims more than the evidence supports.Rarely notes any limit. Treats guesses as facts.Overclaims throughout, or presents invented details as fact.
Total:
20 pts total
HOW TO SUBMIT

Write your essay in Word and save it to your OneDrive folder. Then open this assignment in Canvas, choose the OneDrive tab, select your file, and submit.

M365 reminder: name your file like this: LastName_FirstName_Q4Capstone_WHSP. Save it in Optima → History → WorldHistory_Spring. Name your sources in footnotes (M365 Skill You’re Practicing: Inserting a Footnote in Word).

If you chose to work with a group in the module introduction, submit one shared essay and list every group member’s name under the title. Otherwise, write alone. Both paths use the same rubric.

MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: A Smaller World: Quarter 4 Capstone
Survey · 3 questions · not graded
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
Before you start

Welcome to A Smaller World: Quarter 4 Capstone. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Compare the claims against state power made in South Africa, the American South, and Yugoslavia.
  • Describe how oil, terror, and fast communication tied the world more closely together.
  • Weigh whether a smaller world leaves free peoples safer or more exposed, and finish the Quarter 4 Capstone.

questions.text: Before you read: Does a smaller world make free peoples safer or more exposed? Give your first answer in two or three sentences. You will answer it again at the end of the module, so it is fine if your answer changes.
I have read this module's goals and I know what I am working toward this week.

answers.text: Yes, I have read them
Not yet, I will read them before the first lesson

questions.text: You may do this week’s main assignment alone or with a group. If you choose a group, you agree to the Group Covenant and to submit one shared piece. Which do you choose?

answers.text: I will work alone
I will work with a group and I agree to the Group Covenant

quizzes.title: 28.10 Quarter 4 Exam
quizzes.description:
QUARTER EXAM
Quarter 4 Exam
Exam · 20 questions · 40 points
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
Before you start

This exam covers Quarter 4 only. It has 20 multiple-choice questions worth 2 points each, 40 points in all. Read each question carefully and choose the best answer.

HOW TO WORK
Look back over the quarter's lessons and primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then answer the questions below.

questions.text: In May 1940 the best French and British armies moved north into Belgium. Why was this a mistake?

answers.text: Belgium had already surrendered, so the armies had no one left to meet there
It was what the German plan wanted, with the main thrust in the Ardennes
The Maginot Line was left with no soldiers to defend it against attack
The German tanks were far better and more numerous than the Allied tanks

questions.text: Why did Winston Churchill become prime minister on May 10, 1940?

answers.text: Parliament voted Churchill into office by a large majority after a debate
Chamberlain died suddenly in office and the whole cabinet chose his successor
The King chose Churchill over the objections of Chamberlain and Halifax
Chamberlain resigned after the failure in Norway and Lord Halifax declined the post

questions.text: Why did Japan’s leaders decide in 1941 to go to war with the United States?

answers.text: An oil embargo threatened their fleet, and they would not leave China
The United States had declared war on Japan in July 1941
Germany had ordered Japan to attack Hawaii at once
Japan believed that one great sea battle would win the whole war

questions.text: How did the Americans know to wait for the Japanese at Midway?

answers.text: A Japanese deserter told Admiral Nimitz the plan in Hawaii
Search planes spotted the Japanese fleet two days before the battle
Codebreakers read the Japanese code and learned that the target “AF” was Midway
Radar on Midway tracked the Japanese carriers for hundreds of miles

questions.text: How was the German Sixth Army trapped at Stalingrad?

answers.text: The Soviets flooded the Volga River and cut off the army’s supplies of food
Soviet armies broke the Romanian flanks, and Hitler refused to let Paulus break out
British bombers destroyed the railways that carried its food and ammunition
Paulus was told to retreat to the west, but his own soldiers refused to go

questions.text: According to “The Holocaust: Wannsee and What the Allies Knew”, what was the Wannsee Conference?

answers.text: The meeting at which Hitler first decided to kill all of the Jews of Europe
A secret trial of Jewish leaders held by the SS
The conference at which the Allies first learned of the camps
The moment when state officials agreed to organize killing already under way

questions.text: The Potsdam Declaration of July 1945 called on Japan to surrender. What did it leave unsaid?

answers.text: What would become of the emperor
That Japan would have to give up Manchuria
That the Soviet Union would enter the war against Japan
That an atomic bomb was ready to be used

questions.text: How did the Nuremberg tribunal answer the charge that crimes against peace were an ex post facto law?

answers.text: The Reichstag had passed the law in 1935, before the war began, and it still applied
The tribunal dropped the charge of crimes against peace and tried only war crimes
Germany had signed the Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928 giving up war
The victors had the right to make whatever law they pleased after winning

questions.text: Why does each permanent member of the UN Security Council hold a veto?

answers.text: The founders wanted every nation to have an equal vote in the Council
The great powers would not join without it, so it limits the UN
The American Senate required it before it would approve the charter
It allows the General Assembly to overrule any decision of the Council

questions.text: Why did the Western powers introduce a new currency, the Deutsche Mark, in June 1948?

answers.text: To pay for the costs of the Marshall Plan in all of Europe and the East
To force the Soviets out of their sector of Berlin by cutting its trade
To punish Germany for the cost of the war by forcing it onto a harder money
To stop inflation and restart trade in the Western zones

questions.text: Why was the Warsaw Pact formed in May 1955?

answers.text: West Germany had joined NATO five days earlier
Yugoslavia had left the Soviet camp and the others feared more breaks
The Marshall Plan had ended, so the East needed a new plan
Stalin had died and his successors wanted a new alliance

questions.text: Why could the Soviet Union not veto the United Nations vote to defend South Korea in 1950?

answers.text: The Soviet Union had agreed to the vote in a secret meeting
The Soviet Union had been expelled from the Security Council
Its delegate was boycotting the Council over the seating of China
The vote was taken in the General Assembly, where no one has a veto

questions.text: What was the secret part of the bargain that ended the Cuban missile crisis?

answers.text: The United States would end its embargo on Cuba at once
The American Jupiter missiles in Turkey would be removed within a few months
The United States would give up its place in Berlin
Castro would be removed from power within a year

questions.text: Why did the partition of India in 1947 lead to such suffering?

answers.text: Gandhi had called on his followers to use violence against the Muslims
The Muslim League refused to accept any border at all and would not talk
A judge who had never been to India drew the borders in about five weeks
Britain stayed on to enforce the new border with its own army and police

questions.text: Why did Britain and France stop their attack on Egypt on November 6, 1956?

answers.text: Soviet troops landed in Egypt to defend the canal and its people
Eisenhower opposed it and the United States refused to help the British pound
Israel left the Sinai, and Britain and France lost their excuse to stay
Nasser agreed to hand the canal back to its old owners and to pay for it

questions.text: Which pair correctly names Gorbachev’s two policies?

answers.text: Perestroika, which restructured the economy, and glasnost, which allowed criticism and free speech
Detente, which eased tensions, and perestroika, which allowed free elections
Glasnost, which opened the Soviet economy, and detente, which allowed free speech
Perestroika, which allowed free speech, and glasnost, which allowed private farms

questions.text: How did the Berlin Wall open on November 9, 1989?

answers.text: Gorbachev ordered the wall torn down after a long speech in Moscow
East German soldiers joined the crowd and pulled the wall down with tractors
West and East Germany signed a treaty that night to open the border
A spokesman misread his notes on travel rules, and guards with no orders opened the gates

questions.text: How did the coup against Gorbachev in August 1991 fail?

answers.text: Gorbachev crushed it with loyal troops that he brought from the Crimea
Yeltsin called the people to resist, and the army would not fire
The Communist Party voted it down at a hurried meeting in Moscow
The hardliners lost the support of the Moscow police and the courts

questions.text: Which statement about Mandela’s presidency fits “Moral Claims Against State Power: Mandela, King, and the Balkans”?

answers.text: He jailed the leaders of the old government for their crimes
He served three terms and changed the constitution to stay in office
His government set up a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, and he served one term
He refused to take part in talks with President de Klerk

questions.text: After the September 11 attacks, NATO did something it had never done before. What was it?

answers.text: It sent troops into Pakistan to capture bin Laden
It voted to expel the Taliban government from the alliance
It asked the United Nations to take command of the war
It treated the attack on one member as an attack on all

discussions.title: 28.8 Discussion: Safer or more exposed?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Safer or more exposed?
What a smaller world gives free peoples, and what it costs them.
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Does a smaller world make free peoples safer or more exposed?

Choose one answer. Use your two lists. Name two items from the lists, with dates, that support your answer. Then name one item that belongs on both lists, and explain how the same thing can make a free people stronger and weaker at once.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Write plainly and with respect about the people who died on September 11 and in the wars that followed. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on courtesy. How should a free people treat its opponents and its neighbors when the stakes are high? Say what you think and why.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
Your claim and your reasons
6 pts		Takes a clear side, uses the specific evidence the prompt asks for, and explains why it supports the claim.Takes a side but gives general reasons, or leaves out part of what the prompt asks for.No post, or no claim.
Your reply to a classmate
4 pts		Answers one classmate's actual reasoning. Strengthens it or says where it falls short, politely and with a reason.Replies, but only to agree or disagree with no reason.No reply.
10 pts total
